description:
fixtures2/behavior/map_enumerable.fz via interp exits nonzero at HEAD 89db749f6 (2026-08-21):

  fz2 interp: backend callable construction 1 member target 71 publishes 1 semantic input layouts for arity 2

Raised by ConstructionInputEncoder::encode, src/ir_interp/backend.rs:2036 -- the guard comparing member.target_inputs.len() against target.key.activation.input_len(types). The construction wrapper describes ONE semantic input for a target whose activation has TWO. run and build lanes are green; interp only.

PROVENANCE: that assertion was introduced by fz-k22.23 (8cb9b7a90, 2026-07-14, 'preserve producer callable constructions behind one public ABI'), so it PREDATES the fz-gk4 arity work (89db749f6) and is not fallout from it. Confirmed by git log -L on the line range.

fz-6fr ('map_enumerable crashes all backends: ValueId(6) must be runtime-materializable, value=Absent, native.rs:3375') is CLOSED and that failure is genuinely gone -- two backends recovered and the message changed. This is the successor failure on the one remaining lane, not a reopen: different mechanism, different layer (interp construction encoding vs native materialization).

The disagreement is between the construction wrapper's published input layouts and the target activation's semantic arity -- one of the two is wrong about the call surface. Establish which side is authoritative before patching the guard; per the one-authority principle the fix belongs wherever the call surface is decided, not at the comparison.

REPRO: cargo test --test fixture_matrix -- --test-threads=1 map_enumerable

comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED -- draft PR 90, commit 30e9673c9 on fz-km1/sparse-semantic-inputs.

ROOT CAUSE: ConstructionInputEncoder::encode (ir_interp/backend.rs:2033) required one published input layout per semantic input. target_inputs is SPARSE -- an input the target never reads carries no runtime demand and gets no layout -- which is exactly why every BackendSemanticInputLayout carries its own semantic_index. A dense positional list would have no use for that field.

THE SHAPE THAT TRIPS IT: Enumerable.slice/1's slicer, map.fz:27 -- fn (_map) -> to_list(map) end. Ignores its parameter, answers from its capture. Two semantic inputs, one published layout. Dump from the reduced repro: capture_semantic_inputs [0], surface_semantic_inputs [1], target_inputs one entry at semantic_index 0.

THE GUARD CONTRADICTED ITS OWN FUNCTION. Twelve lines below it the same encoder already reads the list sparsely: iterates self.target.semantic_inputs, finds each layout by .find(|input| input.semantic_index == binding.semantic_index), and skips entries with empty reprs. It never wanted a dense list. Every other consumer agrees -- native (jobs/native.rs:551-560 sizes from the list's own max index and looks up by key), transport_contract_test.rs, artifact_test.rs. The density assumption existed in exactly one place.

FIX: replaced with the invariant that holds -- every published semantic_index is < arity, which is what keeps the by-key lookups and the semantic_values/explicit_values indexing sound. +13/-6, one guard.

TDD: compiler2_jit_and_backend_interp_agree_on_a_callable_that_ignores_its_argument. Nine-line repro; JIT green and interp erroring at HEAD with the ticketed message, both agreeing after. NOTE for anyone re-deriving this: the closure must travel inside a tuple and be destructured to trip it -- an ignored parameter alone reproduces nothing.

RESULT: map_enumerable green on all three lanes (it was down to interp alone). Matrix 4 red -> 3; survivors fz-qe0 and fz-f98.14 (blocked), both pre-existing.

ELIXIR: map_enumerable is an oracle fixture. Ran fixtures2/behavior/map_enumerable.oracle.exs under the real elixir binary -- fz now reproduces its stdout byte-for-byte on run/interp/build, including the final slicer.(map) line that used to fail.

GATES: lib 1441/0; matrix 407/3 single-threaded; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets 0 warnings; fmt clean.
